newsitem.title: USA: Kmart cautiously optimistic for near term.
newsitem.headline: Kmart cautiously optimistic for near term.

text.p: Kmart Corp, which reported a profitable third quarter, said Wednesday it is encouraged by its progress in cutting costs and remains cautiously optimistic for the near term.

"While much work still needs to be done, we are encouraged by our progress in executing our merchandising and operational initiatives through the first nine months of 1996," said Floyd Hall, Kmart chairman and president, in a statement.
"Our biggest challenge of the year lies just ahead in the fourth quarter, and we remain cautiously optimistic about our near-term outlook," Hall said.

Kmart reported a profit for its third quarter ended October 30, 1996 of $9 million or $0.02 a share compared with a net loss of $69 million or $0.15 in the same period a year ago. Total sales for the quarter fell 1.6 percent from last year to $7.85 billion. On a comparable store basis, sales rose 0.1 percent and sales for U.S. Kmart stores increased 0.8 percent.

Gross margin for the third quarter of 1996 was 22.6 percent of sales versus 21.2 percent last year, reflecting fewer markdowns related to the clearance of aged inventory and a lower level of overall promotional activity, Kmart said.

"Comparable sales results for the third quarter were marginally positive; however, they did not meet our growth expectations," Hall said. "Savings from reduced expenses in our operating stores, together with other one-time initiatives, such as closed stores and outsourcing activities, have resulted in a $370 million reduction in SG&A (selling, general and administrative) expense for 1996 year to date."
"Together with the improvement in our gross margin rate, we are beginning to see meaningful progress toward a recovery," he said.

Hall and Warren Flick, president and chief operating officer of U.S. Kmart stores, are scheduled to appear later today at the opening of the retailer's second store in the borough of Manhattan in New York city.

Yesterday, the price of Kmart's stock rose sharply in active trading on market rumors that the retailer may be the target of a takeover by buyout firm Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co. Kmart and KKR declined to comment on the rumors.
Shares of Kmart added 1-5/8 to close at 11-1/4 yesterday on turnover of almost 15 million shares.
Kmart, the second largest retailer in the U.S., operates 2,143 Kmart and 168 Builders Square retail outlets, and operates 129 stores internationally.
